title: MATH 06-02 Mastery Challenge: Prismoidal Formula, Spherical Segments/Wedges, Torus & Spheroids

questions.promptText: What is the volume of a Torus formed by revolving a circle of radius $r = 2\text{ cm}$ around an axis $R = 8\text{ cm}$ from its center?
What is the surface area of a spherical zone of height $h = 4\text{ cm}$ on a sphere of radius $R = 10\text{ cm}$?
What solid of revolution is generated by rotating an ellipse about its MAJOR axis?
questions.explanation: Revolving an ellipse about its major axis creates an elongated prolate spheroid with volume $\frac{4}{3}\pi a b^2$.

questions.promptText: A prismatoid has end areas $A_1 = 20\text{ m}^2, A_2 = 40\text{ m}^2$, midsection area $A_m = 28\text{ m}^2$, and length $L = 12\text{ m}$. What is its volume using the Prismoidal Formula?
Find the volume of a spherical wedge with central dihedral angle $\theta = 30^\circ$ on a sphere of radius $R = 6\text{ cm}$.
What is the total surface area of a Torus with tube radius $r = 4\text{ cm}$ and ring radius $R = 12\text{ cm}$?
Find the volume of a triaxial ellipsoid with semi-axes $a = 3\text{ cm}, b = 4\text{ cm}$, and $c = 5\text{ cm}$.
questions.explanation:
$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi a b c = \frac{4}{3}\pi (3)(4)(5) = 4\pi(20) = 80\pi \approx 251.327\text{ cm}^3$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $4 \times 4 \times 5 \times \pi = 80\pi$.

questions.promptText: What is the volume of a spherical cap (one-base segment) of height $h = 3\text{ cm}$ on a sphere of radius $R = 9\text{ cm}$?
What is the surface area of a spherical lune with angle $\theta = 45^\circ$ on a sphere of radius $R = 8\text{ cm}$?
Find the volume of a spherical segment of two bases with base radii $a = 4\text{ cm}, b = 5\text{ cm}$, and height $h = 3\text{ cm}$.
What is the volume of an oblate spheroid formed by revolving an ellipse with semi-axes $a = 9\text{ cm}$ (equatorial) and $b = 4\text{ cm}$ (polar) about its minor axis?
Which ancient theorem calculates the volume of a solid of revolution as the generating cross-sectional area multiplied by the distance traveled by its centroid?
questions.explanation: Pappus of Alexandria (c. 290–350 A.D.) formulated the two centroid theorems for surface areas and volumes of revolution.

questions.promptText: Why CANNOT the midsection area $A_m$ in the prismoidal formula be computed simply as the arithmetic average $\frac{A_1 + A_2}{2}$?
questions.choiceA: Because the formula is only approximate
questions.choiceB: Because the bases are not parallel
questions.choiceC: Because area scales quadratically with linear dimensions, so $A_m$ must be evaluated using the averaged linear dimensions
questions.choiceD: Because the lateral faces are curved
questions.explanation: Area is non-linear ($L^2$); dimensions at the midpoint must be averaged first before calculating midsection area $A_m$.

questions.promptText: Find the volume of a spherical sector generated by a spherical zone of height $h = 2\text{ cm}$ in a sphere of radius $R = 6\text{ cm}$.
questions.explanation:
$V = \frac{1}{3} A_{\text{zone}} R = \frac{1}{3}(2\pi R h) R = \frac{2}{3}\pi R^2 h = \frac{2}{3}\pi (36)(2) = 48\pi \approx 150.796\text{ cm}^3$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{2}{3} \times 36 \times 2 \times \pi = 48\pi$.

questions.promptText: What is the volume of a spherical pyramid having a base with spherical excess $E = 54^\circ$ on a sphere of radius $R = 10\text{ cm}$?
If the volume of a sphere is $288\pi\text{ cm}^3$, what is its total surface area?
questions.explanation:
$V = \frac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 288\pi \implies R^3 = 216 \implies R = 6\text{ cm}$. Area $A = 4\pi R^2 = 4\pi(36) = 144\pi \approx 452.389\text{ cm}^2$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $4 \times 36 \times \pi = 144\pi$.

questions.promptText: What shape best approximates the true geometric figure of planet Earth?
questions.choiceC: Oblate Spheroid (Flattened at poles, bulging at equator)
questions.explanation: Due to centrifugal rotation, Earth bulges at the equator and is flattened at the poles, forming an oblate spheroid.

questions.promptText: A swimming pool has a rectangular cross-section whose bottom slopes uniformly from a shallow end depth of $1\text{ m}$ to a deep end depth of $3\text{ m}$. If the pool is $25\text{ m}$ long and $10\text{ m}$ wide, what is its volume?
questions.explanation:
Average depth $= (1 + 3)/2 = 2\text{ m}$. Volume $= 25 \times 10 \times 2 = 500\text{ m}^3$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $250 \times 2 = 500\text{ m}^3$.

questions.promptText: A prolate spheroid has major semi-axis $a = 12\text{ cm}$ and minor semi-axis $b = 3\text{ cm}$. Find its volume.
What is the ratio of the volume of a sphere of radius $R$ to the volume of its circumscribing right circular cylinder (Archimedes' famous ratio)?
questions.explanation: Cylinder has height $2R$ and radius $R$: $V_{\text{cyl}} = \pi R^2 (2R) = 2\pi R^3$. Ratio $= \frac{4/3 \pi R^3}{2\pi R^3} = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.promptText: Find the volume of a torus if the cross-sectional circle has diameter $4\text{ cm}$ ($r = 2$) and the mean diameter of the torus ring is $20\text{ cm}$ ($R = 10$).
A spherical tank of radius $R = 5\text{ m}$ is filled with oil to a depth of $h = 2\text{ m}$. What is the volume of the oil in the tank?
questions.explanation:
$V = \frac{\pi h^2}{3}(3R - h) = \frac{\pi (4)}{3}(15 - 2) = \frac{4\pi(13)}{3} = \frac{52\pi}{3} \approx 54.454\text{ m}^3$.

⚡ Speed Shortcut: $\frac{4 \times 13}{3}\pi = \frac{52\pi}{3} \approx 54.45\text{ m}^3$.
